task: Grayscale restoration of handwritten optical digits from additive Gaussian pixel noise
dataset: scikit-learn load_digits, pixel intensities divided by 16
parent: One distinct original digit image. All noisy copies share its split. Writer IDs unavailable.
comparison: Vanilla and distilled students share initial tensors, minibatches, noise and optimizer. Train one frozen supervised teacher per seed on the same training parents. Long supervised control has 720 updates; FLOPs differ across arms.
training_loss: MSE to clean image for teacher and supervised student. Distilled student uses 0.5 MSE to clean image and 0.5 MSE to frozen teacher output. No teacher at student inference.
evaluation: One fixed noisy realization per held-out image, shared by all models and training seeds. Noisy input and evaluated prediction clipped to [0,1]. Training uses the [0,1] clean reference and the raw frozen teacher output. Mean per-image PSNR, horizontal and vertical first-difference MAE. No checkpoint or hyperparameter selection.
primary_contrast: Distilled minus vanilla student, both at step 240. Resample original test images, pairing arms and all seeds; intervals condition on the three trained pairs.
interpretation: All gates required for a positive pilot signal on this dataset. The thresholds are study choices, not a field standard. Report each result regardless of sign. Long supervision, identity input and teacher scores are descriptive controls. No claim of generalization to a new device, writer population, or signal modality.
